1.title: My pet peeves
1.brief: Write a paragraph about the habits that get on your nerves. Use it-clauses with “when” to react to them and relative clauses to describe the people involved.
1.briefEs: Escribe un párrafo sobre los hábitos que te molestan usando cláusulas con “it… when” y cláusulas relativas.
criteria: Three it-clauses with when (It bothers me when…, I can’t stand it when…).
Two relative clauses, one with the pronoun omitted (the people I live with).
Use “pet peeve” and “to get on someone’s nerves”.
1.model: Everybody has pet peeves, and I have quite a few. It really bothers me when people talk on the phone in the cinema. I also can't stand it when someone eats my food from the fridge without asking. The person I share a flat with does this all the time, and it gets on my nerves. Another thing is unpunctuality. It drives me crazy when friends who promise to arrive at eight turn up at nine without a message. On the other hand, I love it when people are considerate. A colleague who brings coffee for everyone on Monday morning is my hero! I think small details like these show who you can really trust.

1.title: A reference for a friend
1.brief: A friend is applying to share a flat. Write a short reference describing his or her personality and why he or she would be a good flatmate.
1.briefEs: Escribe una carta de referencia describiendo la personalidad de un amigo como buen compañero de vivienda.
criteria: Four personality adjectives from the unit (reliable, considerate, trustworthy…).
Three relative clauses with who, that or which.
Formal opening and closing (To whom it may concern / Yours faithfully).
1.model:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to recommend Felipe Rodríguez, who has been my friend and flatmate for three years. Felipe is one of the most reliable people that I know. He always pays the bills on time and he never forgets the cleaning rota. He is also very considerate: he keeps the music low when people are studying and he always asks before inviting guests. It is something I really appreciate when people respect shared spaces. He is trustworthy, too. When I travelled for two months, he looked after my plants and my cat, which was not easy! I am sure he would be an excellent flatmate.

Yours faithfully,
Laura Medina

1.title: The person I look up to
1.brief: Write a blog post about someone you look up to. Explain who the person is and describe a moment when you understood why you admire them.
1.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de blog sobre alguien a quien admiras y un momento en que entendiste por qué.
criteria: Use “to look up to” and one more phrase from the unit.
Two relative clauses, one used as an object with the pronoun omitted.
One it-clause with when (It amazed me when…).
1.model: The person I look up to most is my older sister, Camila. She is a nurse who works night shifts at a public hospital in Bogotá. For years I didn't understand why she chose such a difficult job. Then, last year, my grandfather became very ill. Camila was the one who explained everything to the family calmly. It amazed me when she stayed awake for two days to help him. The patience she showed was incredible. She never complains about the people she works with, even when they drive her crazy. She is the kind of person everybody wants as a friend. Today I'm studying medicine, and that is because of her.

2.title: Learning online or in a classroom?
2.brief: Compare learning a language online and in a classroom. Give your opinion and support it with comparisons.
2.briefEs: Compara aprender un idioma en línea y en un salón de clase, y da tu opinión.
criteria: Start one sentence with a gerund phrase as subject (Studying online is…).
Five comparisons with adjectives, nouns and verbs (more flexible, fewer, as much as).
Use “advantage / drawback” and “by far” or “nowhere near”.
2.model: Learning a language is time-consuming, so choosing the right method is important. Studying online is far more flexible than going to a classroom: you can study at midnight if you want. It is also cheaper, and you waste less time travelling. However, the biggest drawback is motivation. Students who study alone usually practise less than students in a group, and they speak nowhere near as much. In a classroom, you get more feedback and you make friends. Talking to real people is by far the best way to lose your fear. In my opinion, the ideal option is a mix: online lessons for grammar and vocabulary, and face-to-face classes for speaking. That way you get the advantages of both.

2.title: Why I gave up social media
2.brief: Write a short article about a habit you gave up or took up. Explain why and compare your life before and after.
2.briefEs: Escribe un artículo corto sobre un hábito que dejaste o empezaste, comparando tu vida antes y después.
criteria: Two gerund phrases as subject and two as object.
Three comparisons (less stressed than, as … as, more time).
Use “to give up” or “to take up” and “worthwhile”.
2.model: Last year I decided to give up social media for six months. Scrolling through Instagram was taking up two hours of my day, and comparing my life with other people's made me feel worse. At first, not checking my phone was harder than I expected. But after a month, I felt much less stressed than before. I slept better and I read more books than in the previous two years. I also took up running, which I enjoy far more than watching videos. My friendships improved too: meeting people in person is not as convenient as sending messages, but it is much more worthwhile. Now I use social media again, but I spend nowhere near as much time on it.

2.title: Two jobs, one choice
2.brief: You have two job offers. Write an email to a friend comparing them and asking for advice.
2.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo comparando dos ofertas de trabajo y pidiéndole consejo.
criteria: Six comparisons, including “the same as” or “similar to”.
One gerund phrase as subject (Working from home sounds…).
Ask for advice with a question at the end.
2.model:
Hi Sebas,

I need your advice! I've got two job offers. The first is at a big bank. The salary is higher and the office is closer to my flat, but I would work longer hours than now. The second is at a small startup. The pay is lower, but it is far more flexible: working from home three days a week sounds amazing. The team is younger and the work seems more creative. Both jobs are similar to my current one, but the startup offers more training. On the other hand, the bank is more stable than a startup, and I'm worried about that. Taking a risk is not easy at my age! Which one would you choose?

Talk soon,
Diana

3.title: A favour from a colleague
3.brief: You need a colleague to cover your work for two days. Write a polite email asking for help and explaining the situation.
3.briefEs: Escribe un correo cortés pidiendo a un colega que cubra tu trabajo por dos días.
criteria: Three different request forms: Would you mind + -ing, I was wondering if, Would it be possible to…
One indirect question (Do you know whether…).
Use “to be tied up”, “appreciate” or “by any chance”.
3.model:
Hi Marcela,

I hope you're well. I'm writing because I have a family emergency and I need to travel to Pasto on Thursday and Friday. I was wondering if you could take care of my clients for those two days. Would you mind answering my emails and checking the orders? I know you're tied up with the new campaign, so please tell me if it's too much. Would it be possible to have a quick meeting tomorrow so I can explain everything? I'd also like to know whether you are free on Monday morning, by any chance, so I can thank you with a coffee. I really appreciate your help.

Best,
Óscar

3.title: Asking for information
3.brief: Write a formal email to a university or language school asking about a course. Use indirect questions throughout.
3.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal a una universidad pidiendo información sobre un curso con preguntas indirectas.
criteria: Five indirect questions with statement word order.
Use “whether” in at least one question.
Formal register: no contractions, Dear Sir or Madam, Yours faithfully.
3.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am interested in the Advanced English Writing course advertised on your website, and I would be grateful if you could send me some further information. Firstly, could you tell me when the next course starts? I would also like to know how many students there are in each group. I was wondering whether the classes are offered in the evening, as I work during the day. In addition, could you let me know if there is a placement test and how much it costs? Finally, I would appreciate it if you could tell me whether a certificate is awarded at the end of the course.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Andrea Salazar

3.title: Notes for a new neighbour
3.brief: A new family has moved in next door. Write a friendly note introducing yourself and making two requests politely.
3.briefEs: Escribe una nota amable a los vecinos nuevos presentándote y haciéndoles dos peticiones.
criteria: Use a request with an if-clause (I'd be grateful if you could…).
Use “Would you mind + -ing” once.
Offer help with “Don’t hesitate to…”.
3.model:
Dear neighbours,

Welcome to the building! My name is Ricardo and I live in 501, just above you. I hope you are settling in well. I have a small favour to ask. I work night shifts, so I sleep in the mornings. I'd be grateful if you could keep the noise down before 11 a.m., especially on weekdays. Also, would you mind not leaving bags of rubbish in the corridor? The building has a special area downstairs. I know moving house is stressful, so if you need anything, like a drill or a ladder, don't hesitate to knock on my door. I'm happy to give you a hand.

Best wishes,
Ricardo

4.title: A journey that went wrong
4.brief: Write a story about a journey that went wrong. Use the past continuous for background, the simple past for events and the past perfect for earlier events.
4.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre un viaje que salió mal usando pasado continuo, pasado simple y pasado perfecto.
criteria: Two past continuous verbs for background.
Three past perfect verbs (had left, had forgotten).
Use “by the time”, “eventually” and “delay” or “to break down”.
4.model: It was raining heavily when we left Bogotá for the coast. My brother was driving and I was choosing the music. After three hours, the car broke down in the middle of nowhere. We realised that my brother had forgotten to check the oil before the trip. While we were waiting for help, I discovered that I had left my phone charger at home. By the time a mechanic arrived, it was dark and we were starving. The repair took four more hours. Meanwhile, we ate the sandwiches our mother had prepared. Eventually, we arrived at the hotel at two in the morning, but the receptionist had given our room to someone else! It was a trip we will never forget.

4.title: Witness statement
4.brief: You saw an accident or a robbery. Write a witness statement for the police describing what happened in order.
4.briefEs: Escribe una declaración como testigo para la policía describiendo lo que pasó.
criteria: Past continuous for what people were doing when it happened.
Two past perfect verbs to show earlier actions.
Formal, clear sequence: first, then, by the time.
4.model:
Statement of: Carolina Mejía
On Tuesday, 14 March, at about 6:30 p.m., I was standing at the bus stop on Carrera Séptima. It was getting dark and many people were walking home. A man in a grey jacket was looking at the shop windows. Suddenly, he ran into the phone shop and grabbed two phones from the counter. I noticed that he had parked a motorbike outside, because the engine was still running. The shop assistant shouted, but by the time she reached the door, the man had already left. I had seen the motorbike before, at around six o'clock, so I think he had been watching the shop. I wrote down part of the number plate: XYZ 4.

4.title: Why I was late
4.brief: You arrived very late for an important meeting. Write an email to apologise and explain what had happened.
4.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal disculpándote por llegar tarde y explicando lo que había pasado.
criteria: Use the past perfect to explain earlier causes.
Use “while” or “when” with past continuous.
Use a formal apology: I would like to apologise for…
4.model:
Dear Mr. Castro,

I would like to apologise for arriving forty minutes late to this morning's meeting. I had left home with plenty of time, but while I was crossing the city, there was a serious accident on the Avenida Boyacá. The police had closed two lanes, so traffic was barely moving. When I tried to call you, I realised that my phone had died, because I had forgotten to charge it the night before. By the time I arrived, you had already presented the main points. I understand this caused a delay, and I would be happy to meet again tomorrow to go over anything I missed.

Kind regards,
Natalia Pérez

5.title: Customs in my country
5.brief: Write an article for foreign visitors explaining some customs in Colombia: what is expected, acceptable or not acceptable.
5.briefEs: Escribe un artículo para visitantes extranjeros sobre costumbres colombianas: lo esperado y lo inaceptable.
criteria: Use four expressions: it’s the custom to, be (not) supposed to, be expected to, it’s (not) acceptable to.
Two noun phrases with relative clauses (People who visit…, A guest who arrives…).
Use “etiquette” and “to frown on”.
5.model: If you visit Colombia, some local etiquette will help you fit in. When you meet someone, it's the custom to greet them with a handshake or, between women and between friends, a kiss on the cheek. People who are invited to dinner are expected to arrive a little late — arriving exactly on time is not common! It's acceptable to bring a small gift, like wine or dessert. At work, you are supposed to greet everyone in the office when you arrive, not only your boss. Colombians frown on people who don't say "buenos días". A visitor who refuses a cup of coffee may seem rude, so accept at least one. Finally, it's not acceptable to talk about drugs or violence as a joke.

5.title: Advice for an exchange student
5.brief: An exchange student is coming to your city. Write an email explaining the unwritten rules at your school or university.
5.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un estudiante de intercambio explicando las reglas no escritas de tu universidad.
criteria: Three expressions of expectation (supposed to, expected to, acceptable).
Two noun phrases containing relative clauses.
Use “unwritten rule” or “to get away with”.
5.model:
Hi Lukas,

I'm glad you're coming to study here! Let me tell you some unwritten rules. Students who arrive late are not usually punished, but you're expected to apologise to the professor. You're supposed to call professors "profe", which is friendly but respectful. It's acceptable to eat in class, but not hot food! The library is a place where silence is really important, and you can't get away with talking on the phone. Another unwritten rule: the person who has a birthday is expected to bring a cake for the group. Finally, it's the custom to go out for empanadas after exams.

See you soon!
Marta

5.title: A social mistake
5.brief: Write about a time when you or someone you know broke a social rule (in another country or at a family event). Explain what happened and what the rule is.
5.briefEs: Escribe sobre una vez en que tú u otra persona rompió una norma social, y explica cuál es la norma.
criteria: Explain the rule with “be (not) supposed to” or “it’s (not) the custom to”.
Two noun phrases with relative clauses.
Use “to offend”, “appropriate” or “norm”.
5.model: When I first visited Japan, I made a mistake that I still remember. At a restaurant, I left a tip on the table for the waiter who had served us. A few minutes later, he ran after me in the street to return the money! I felt embarrassed. I learned that in Japan you are not supposed to tip; it can even offend people. The norm there is that good service is part of the job. Back home in Colombia, it's the custom to leave ten percent, so it's appropriate for me. The thing I learned from that trip is simple: people who travel should read about local customs before they go.

6.title: A complaint about a faulty product
6.brief: Write a complaint email to an online shop about a product that arrived damaged or stopped working.
6.briefEs: Escribe un correo de reclamo a una tienda en línea sobre un producto que llegó dañado o dejó de funcionar.
criteria: Three past participles as adjectives (cracked, scratched, broken).
Two “need + gerund / passive infinitive” structures.
Use “keep + gerund”, “warranty” and “to replace”.
6.model:
Dear Customer Service,

I am writing to complain about the laptop I ordered from your website on 2 May (order number 45821). When it arrived, the box was damaged and the screen was cracked in one corner. The keyboard is also scratched. In addition, the laptop keeps switching off after ten minutes, so I cannot use it for work. It clearly needs to be repaired, or, better, it needs replacing. As the laptop is still under warranty, I would like you to replace it with a new one or give me a full refund. I have attached photos of the damage. I hope you can solve this problem quickly.

Yours faithfully,
Jorge Ramírez

6.title: Things that need fixing
6.brief: You are moving out of a rented flat. Write a note to the landlord listing problems in the flat and what each one needs.
6.briefEs: Escribe una nota al arrendador con los problemas del apartamento y lo que necesita cada uno.
criteria: Describe five problems with participles or nouns (a leak, a stain, loose, dented).
Use “need + -ing” and “need to be + past participle”.
Use “to wear out” or “faulty”.
6.model:
Dear Mr. Suárez,

Before I move out, I would like to tell you about some problems in the flat. There is a leak under the kitchen sink, so the pipe needs to be repaired. The bathroom door handle is loose and it needs tightening. There is a big stain on the living room carpet; I think it needs cleaning by a professional. The fridge door is dented and the light inside is faulty. Finally, the sofa is worn out and it needs to be replaced soon. The shower keeps dripping, too. I'm sorry I couldn't fix these things myself.

Best regards,
Valentina

6.title: My worst repair experience
6.brief: Tell the story of something that broke and the problems you had getting it fixed.
6.briefEs: Cuenta la historia de algo que se dañó y los problemas que tuviste para arreglarlo.
criteria: Use “keep + gerund” twice.
Use “need + passive infinitive” once.
Three words for damage (cracked, leak, faulty, loose…).
6.model: Last year my washing machine started making a strange noise. Then it kept stopping in the middle of every wash, and water kept leaking onto the floor. I called a technician, who said that one part was faulty and needed to be replaced. He took the old part and promised to come back in two days. He didn't come back for three weeks! Meanwhile, I had to wash my clothes by hand. When he finally returned, he installed the new part, but the door was loose and the glass was cracked. I asked him to fix it, but he said it wasn't his job. In the end, I bought a new machine. Now I always ask for a warranty.

7.title: Changes in my city
7.brief: Write an article for a local website about the changes that are being made in your city or neighbourhood, and their causes and effects.
7.briefEs: Escribe un artículo sobre los cambios que se están haciendo en tu ciudad, con causas y efectos.
criteria: Two passives in the present continuous (is being built) and two in the present perfect (has been opened).
Use due to, as a result of and thanks to.
Two infinitive clauses of purpose (in order to reduce…).
7.model: Our neighbourhood is changing fast. A new metro station is being built on Avenida 68, and several streets are being closed as a result of the work. In the last year, two parks have been renovated and a new library has been opened. Thanks to these projects, families have more places to spend time together. However, not all the effects are positive. Due to the construction, traffic has become terrible, and many small shops have lost customers. The city council has promised that the metro will be finished by 2027. In order to help local businesses, a special fund has been created. In my opinion, the changes are necessary, but they are being done too slowly.

7.title: An update for the team
7.brief: Write an email to your team explaining the status of a project: what is being done, what has been done and why.
7.briefEs: Escribe un correo al equipo explicando el estado de un proyecto: qué se está haciendo y qué se ha hecho.
criteria: Four passive forms in present continuous and present perfect.
Two infinitive phrases (to save time, in order to…).
Use “to be under way”, “ongoing” or “to carry out”.
7.model:
Hi everyone,

Here is a quick update on the website project. The new design has been approved by the director, and the photos have been uploaded. At the moment, the texts are being translated into English in order to reach more international clients. Some tests are being carried out by the IT team to check the speed of the site. Unfortunately, the launch has been delayed due to a problem with the payment system, but the solution is already under way. To save time, I suggest we meet for only fifteen minutes on Monday. The ongoing work should be finished by next Friday.

Thanks for your effort,
Pablo

7.title: A problem and its causes
7.brief: Choose an environmental or social problem in your country. Explain what is causing it and what is being done to solve it.
7.briefEs: Elige un problema ambiental o social y explica qué lo causa y qué se está haciendo para solucionarlo.
criteria: Use three prepositions of cause: due to, because of, as a result of.
Two passives in the present continuous or present perfect.
Use “to affect” and “consequence” correctly.
7.model: Deforestation in the Amazon is one of Colombia's most serious problems. Thousands of hectares have been lost in the last ten years, mainly due to cattle farming and illegal mining. As a result of this destruction, many animals have lost their habitat, and the climate in the whole region is being affected. One consequence is that rivers are becoming dry in some months. Fortunately, some things are being done. Protected areas have been created, and local communities are being paid to look after the forest. In my opinion, these programmes are a good start, but more needs to be done in order to stop the problem completely.

8.title: City or countryside?
8.brief: Would you rather live in a big city or in the countryside? Give your preference and explain how you would make your life work there.
8.briefEs: ¿Preferirías vivir en la ciudad o en el campo? Da tu preferencia y explica cómo lo harías funcionar.
criteria: Use “would rather” and “would prefer” correctly (would rather + base form, would prefer + to).
Three “by + gerund” structures for methods.
Use “instead of” or “to be keen on”.
8.model: If I could choose, I would rather live in the countryside than in a big city. I would prefer to wake up to birds instead of car horns. Some people think rural life is boring, but I'm keen on nature and quiet places. Of course, I would need to work, so I would make money by working online as a translator. I would stay healthy by growing my own vegetables and by walking every day. The only problem would be loneliness, but I would solve it by joining community activities and by inviting friends from the city on weekends. I would rather have a simple life than a stressful one.

8.title: How to save money
8.brief: Write a blog post with practical tips for students who want to save money. Explain the method for each tip.
8.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de blog con consejos prácticos para que los estudiantes ahorren dinero.
criteria: Five “by + gerund” structures.
One sentence with “would rather” and one with “would prefer”.
Use “to cut down on” and “to work out”.
8.model: Being a student is expensive, but you can save a lot by making small changes. First, work out how much you spend every month by writing down every purchase for two weeks. You'll be surprised! Second, cut down on eating out. You can save up to 200,000 pesos a month by cooking at home and by taking lunch to university. Third, save on transport by cycling or walking short distances. Many students would rather take a taxi, but a bike is cheaper and healthier. Finally, avoid expensive subscriptions by sharing them with friends. Personally, I would prefer to have one streaming service than five that I never use. Saving gradually is better than not saving at all.

8.title: Choosing a holiday
8.brief: Your friend has suggested a beach holiday. Write an email saying you would prefer something different and explain how you could organise it.
8.briefEs: Escribe un correo diciendo que preferirías otro tipo de vacaciones y explica cómo organizarlas.
criteria: Use would rather (not) and would prefer (not) to.
Two “by + gerund” structures.
One expression: to be worth it, means, method.
8.model:
Hi Juli,

Thanks for the idea of going to Santa Marta! But to be honest, I'd rather not spend another holiday on a hot beach. I'd prefer to do something more active this time. What about hiking in the Cocora Valley? I would rather sleep in a small cabin than in a big hotel. We could save money by sharing a room and by cooking our own meals. We can get there easily by taking a bus to Salento, then a jeep. I know it's colder, but I'm sure it'll be worth it. I'd prefer not to go in December because it's so crowded. What do you think?

Love,
Mafe

9.title: Getting things done
9.brief: You are preparing your flat for a family visit. Write an email to a friend saying what you have had or are getting done by professionals.
9.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre lo que mandaste hacer o vas a mandar hacer en tu apartamento.
criteria: Four “have / get + object + past participle” structures in different tenses.
Use “quote / estimate” and “to service” or “to install”.
One sentence asking for advice.
9.model:
Hi Simón,

My parents are coming from Spain next month, so I'm getting my flat ready. Last week I had the walls painted and I got the windows cleaned. It was expensive, but it looks great! Tomorrow I'm having a new shower installed, because the old one was terrible. I also need to get the air conditioning serviced. I asked for two quotes: one company wants 300,000 pesos and the other 180,000. Have you ever had your AC fixed? Which company did you use? I'm also going to get my car washed before I pick them up at the airport.

Speak soon,
Lorena

9.title: Ideas for a better office
9.brief: Your manager asks for ideas to improve the office or classroom. Write a short proposal with suggestions using different structures.
9.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta corta con sugerencias para mejorar la oficina o el salón usando distintas estructuras.
criteria: Five suggestions with different forms: How about + -ing, Why don’t we, Maybe we could, One option is to, Have you thought about + -ing.
One negative question for a suggestion (Wouldn’t it be better to…?).
Use “worth a try” or “to go ahead”.
9.model:
Proposal: improving our office

After talking to the team, I would like to make some suggestions. First, how about creating a quiet room for people who need to concentrate? Many of us find the open space too noisy. Second, why don't we buy a few plants? It is a cheap idea, and research shows that plants make people happier. Maybe we could also change the lights near the windows, because they are too bright in the afternoon. One option is to have the coffee machine repaired instead of buying a new one. Have you thought about allowing people to work from home on Fridays? Wouldn't it be better to try it for one month first? I think these ideas are worth a try. If you agree, we can go ahead next week.

9.title: Talk me out of it
9.brief: Write a dialogue between two friends. One wants to do something risky (quit a job, buy an expensive car). The other makes suggestions to talk him or her out of it.
9.briefEs: Escribe un diálogo donde un amigo intenta convencer al otro de no hacer algo arriesgado con sugerencias.
criteria: Four suggestions in different forms (Why don’t you…? You could… What about…?).
One sentence with “get / have something done”.
Use “to talk someone into / out of”.
9.model:
Andrés: I've decided. I'm quitting my job tomorrow to travel around Asia.
Paula: Wait! Why don't you think about it for a week first?
Andrés: I've thought about it for months.
Paula: OK, but what about asking your boss for unpaid leave instead? You could travel for three months and come back.
Andrés: Hmm. That's not a bad idea.
Paula: And have you had your passport renewed? It expired last year, remember?
Andrés: Oh no, I forgot! I need to get it done.
Paula: See? Why not plan everything properly? Maybe you could save a bit more money first.
Andrés: You're trying to talk me out of it!
Paula: No, I'm trying to talk you into doing it well!

10.title: My life in 2040
10.brief: Write about how you imagine your life and the world in 2040. Use will, the future continuous and the future perfect.
10.briefEs: Escribe cómo imaginas tu vida y el mundo en 2040 con will, futuro continuo y futuro perfecto.
criteria: Two future continuous verbs (will be living).
Three future perfect verbs (will have finished).
Use “by then” and “to be likely to”.
10.model: In 2040 I will be 42 years old. By then, I will have finished my master's degree and I will have worked in at least two countries. I imagine I will be living in a small house near the sea, and I will probably be working from home as a software engineer. I hope I will have started a family by that time. The world will also be very different. Most people will be driving electric cars, and many jobs will have disappeared because of artificial intelligence. Cities are likely to be hotter, so I think we will be spending more time indoors. However, I'm optimistic. I think we will have found solutions to some of the biggest environmental problems.

10.title: A timeline of my studies
10.brief: Write a short professional profile describing your education and work history. Use time expressions correctly.
10.briefEs: Escribe un perfil profesional corto con tu historial de estudios y trabajo usando expresiones de tiempo.
criteria: Use during, in, ago, from … to, for and since.
Mix past simple and present perfect correctly.
One sentence about future goals with “will have”.
10.model: I am a graphic designer from Manizales. I studied design at the National University from 2014 to 2019. During my studies, I worked part-time in a printing shop. In 2019, I moved to Bogotá and got a job at an advertising agency, where I worked for three years. I left that job two years ago to start my own studio. Since then, I have designed logos and websites for more than forty small businesses. I have also been teaching an evening course since 2023. My next milestone is to work with international clients. By the end of next year, I will have opened a small office and I will have hired my first employee.

10.title: Predictions for my city
10.brief: Write an article for a student magazine with predictions about your city in twenty years. Give reasons.
10.briefEs: Escribe un artículo con predicciones sobre tu ciudad en veinte años y da razones.
criteria: Two predictions with will / won’t and one with “be likely to”.
Two future continuous and two future perfect verbs.
Use “eventually” and “for the time being”.
10.model: What will Cali look like in twenty years? First, I think the city will have grown enormously: experts say the population is likely to reach four million. The new train to Jamundí will have been finished, so thousands of people will be commuting by rail instead of by car. Secondly, the climate will be hotter, and people will be living in buildings with green roofs and gardens. For the time being, salsa is the city's identity, and I don't think that will change. Eventually, Cali will become a centre for technology, and young people won't have left for Bogotá or abroad, because they will have good jobs at home.

11.title: A decision I would change
11.brief: Write about an important decision in your past. Explain the sequence of events, what you regret and what would have happened if you had decided differently.
11.briefEs: Escribe sobre una decisión importante, lo que lamentas y qué habría pasado si hubieras decidido distinto.
criteria: Three time clauses (as soon as, once, by the time, until).
Two sentences with should (not) have + past participle.
Two sentences with if + past perfect, would have + participle.
11.model: When I finished school, my parents wanted me to study law. As soon as I started the first semester, I knew it wasn't for me, but I didn't say anything until the third year. By the time I finally told them, I had spent a lot of money and time. I should have been honest from the beginning. I shouldn't have been so afraid of disappointing them. If I had changed to music earlier, I would have saved two years. In hindsight, though, the experience taught me something. Once I started studying music, I realised how important it is to follow your own path. If I hadn't studied law, I wouldn't have met my best friend.

11.title: Plans that fell through
11.brief: Write an email to a friend about a plan (a trip, a party, a business idea) that fell through. Explain the sequence and what you should have done.
11.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre un plan que fracasó, con la secuencia y lo que deberías haber hecho.
criteria: Use “to fall through” and “with hindsight”.
Three time clauses with different conjunctions.
One regret with should have and one with if + past perfect.
11.model:
Hi Kate,

Remember the trip to Peru I told you about? Well, it fell through. The moment I booked the flights, things started to go wrong. Before I could reserve the hotels, my friend Mónica broke her leg. Then, once she had recovered, her company didn't give her the holidays. We waited until the last minute, and by the time we decided to cancel, the airline wouldn't give us our money back. With hindsight, I should have bought travel insurance. If I had checked the cancellation rules, I would have chosen a different ticket. Lesson learned!

Love,
Gabi

11.title: The story of a missed opportunity
11.brief: Write a story (real or invented) about someone who missed a great opportunity. End with what he or she learned.
11.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre alguien que perdió una gran oportunidad y lo que aprendió.
criteria: Four time clauses (before, after, once, the moment, until).
Two third conditional sentences.
Use “to turn down”, “to blame” or “otherwise”.
11.model: Carlos was a talented young footballer from Tumaco. When he was seventeen, a scout from a Brazilian club watched him play. The moment the match ended, the scout offered him a trial in São Paulo. But Carlos turned it down. He didn't want to leave his girlfriend, and he was afraid of living alone. After the scout left, his coach said, "You will regret this." He was right. A year later, Carlos's girlfriend left him, and he injured his knee before he could get another chance. He didn't play professionally until he was twenty-five, and by then it was too late. Carlos doesn't blame anyone. "If I had gone to Brazil, my life would have been different," he says. "Otherwise, I wouldn't be the coach I am now."

12.title: Why I'm learning English
12.brief: Write a paragraph explaining why you are learning English and what you want to use it for.
12.briefEs: Escribe un párrafo explicando por qué aprendes inglés y para qué lo quieres usar.
criteria: Three purpose structures: to + infinitive, so that, for + noun.
Three reason structures: because, since, due to, the reason why.
Use “to justify” or “rationale”.
12.model: There are several reasons why I am learning English. The main reason is my job: I work in tourism, and since most of our clients come from the USA and Europe, I need English to communicate with them. I also want to improve my English so that I can apply for a master's degree in Canada. Due to the high cost of studying abroad, I need a scholarship, and for that I must pass the IELTS exam. Another reason is personal. I love series and books, and I want to enjoy them in the original language. I spend about an hour a day studying, which is easy to justify because English opens so many doors.

12.title: A request for funding
12.brief: Write a formal email to your company or university asking for money for a project or course. Explain the purpose and the reasons.
12.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal solicitando financiación para un proyecto o curso, explicando propósito y razones.
criteria: Use “so that”, “in order to” and “for + noun” for purpose.
Use “owing to”, “due to” and “because of” for reasons.
Formal register and a clear request.
12.model:
Dear Dr. Morales,

I am writing to request financial support of 2,500,000 pesos to attend the International Education Conference in Lima in October. The purpose of the trip is to present our research on bilingual education, so that other universities can learn from our experience. The money would be for the registration fee and accommodation. Owing to recent cuts in the department budget, I am unable to cover these costs myself. Due to the importance of the event, I believe it would be an excellent opportunity for the university. In order to share what I learn, I would organise a workshop for colleagues when I return. The reason I am applying now is that the deadline for registration is 15 August.

Yours sincerely,
Laura Castaño

12.title: What is it for?
12.brief: Describe an invention or app that you think is very useful. Explain what it is intended for and why it became popular.
12.briefEs: Describe un invento o aplicación útil: para qué sirve y por qué se volvió popular.
criteria: Use “to be intended for”, “for + -ing” and “so that”.
Three reason connectors (because of, since, the reason why).
Use “to account for” or “thereby”.
12.model: One app that I find extremely useful is a language exchange app. It is intended for people who want to practise a language with native speakers. You use it for chatting, sending voice messages and even making video calls, so that you can practise speaking without paying for classes. The reason why it became so popular is simple: it's free and fun. Since millions of people use it, you can always find a partner. Because of the pandemic, many people were at home and downloaded it, thereby helping it grow very fast. I think the social aspect accounts for its success: people don't only learn languages, they make friends from all over the world.

13.title: The mystery of the empty office
13.brief: Write a short mystery story. Someone finds an unusual situation and deduces what must, might or can't have happened.
13.briefEs: Escribe una historia de misterio en la que alguien deduce lo que debe, puede o no puede haber pasado.
criteria: Four past modals of certainty (must have, might have, could have, can’t have).
Use “evidence”, “to rule out” and “plausible”.
A clear ending with the solution.
13.model: When Diana arrived at the office on Monday, the door was open, the lights were on and her computer was missing. "Someone must have broken in," she thought. But there was no evidence of a robbery: the window wasn't broken and nothing else had been taken. It can't have been a stranger, because the alarm didn't go off. She ruled out the cleaner, who had been on holiday. "Maybe the IT guy took it for repairs," she thought. That seemed plausible, but he might have left a note. Then she saw a message on her phone from her boss: "Took your laptop home on Friday. Mine crashed. Sorry!" He must have forgotten to lock the door. Diana laughed — and then she was furious.

13.title: What should they have done?
13.brief: Read this situation: “A shop assistant accused a customer of stealing, but the customer was innocent.” Write your opinion about what the people should or shouldn’t have done.
13.briefEs: Opina sobre lo que las personas de una situación deberían o no deberían haber hecho.
criteria: Three past modals for judgments (should have, shouldn’t have, could have).
One past modal for certainty (must have felt).
Use “to give someone the benefit of the doubt” or “negligence”.
13.model: In my opinion, the shop assistant handled the situation badly. First, she shouldn't have accused the customer in front of other people. The customer must have felt terrible and embarrassed. The assistant should have given him the benefit of the doubt and checked the security cameras before saying anything. She could have called the manager or the security guard quietly. On the other hand, the manager should have trained the staff better, so there was some negligence from the shop too. The customer could have complained more strongly, but I think he reacted calmly. Finally, the shop ought to have apologised publicly. A small discount would have been a nice gesture.

13.title: A message about a mistake
13.brief: Something went wrong at a party you organised (food was missing, a guest got lost). Write an email to a friend guessing what happened and saying what you should have done.
13.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo especulando sobre qué salió mal en una fiesta y qué deberías haber hecho.
criteria: Use must have, might have and can’t have for guesses.
Use should have and shouldn’t have for regrets.
Include “presumably” or “to be bound to”.
13.model:
Hi Mario,

What a disaster yesterday! The cake didn't arrive, and I still don't know why. The bakery must have confused the address, because they say it was delivered at 6 p.m. It can't have gone to my flat — I was home all afternoon. It might have gone to the building across the street, which has a similar number. Presumably, someone there enjoyed a free chocolate cake! I should have given them my phone number. I also shouldn't have ordered it so late. Anyway, the guests didn't seem to mind. With so many people, something was bound to go wrong!

See you soon,
Clara

14.title: How it's made
14.brief: Describe the process of making a product you know well (chocolate, a T-shirt, arepas, bread). Use the passive and relative clauses.
14.briefEs: Describe el proceso de fabricación de un producto usando la voz pasiva y cláusulas relativas.
criteria: Six passive verbs describing stages.
One defining and one non-defining relative clause (with commas).
Use “stage”, “raw material” and “quality control”.
14.model: Chocolate is one of the products that Colombia is proud of. The raw material is cacao, which grows on trees in regions like Santander and Huila. At the first stage, the cacao pods are cut from the trees by hand and the beans are removed. Then the beans are fermented for about a week, which develops the flavour. After that, they are dried in the sun and sent to the factory. There, the beans are roasted and ground into a thick paste. Sugar and milk are added, and the mixture is heated and cooled several times. Before the chocolate is packed, quality control is carried out by experts whose job is to taste every batch. Finally, the bars are labelled and sold.

14.title: A recycling guide
14.brief: Write a short guide for your building explaining how rubbish is sorted and what happens to it.
14.briefEs: Escribe una guía corta para tu edificio explicando cómo se clasifica la basura y qué pasa con ella.
criteria: Five present passive verbs.
Two non-defining relative clauses with commas.
Use “to sort”, “to dispose of” and “to be labelled”.
14.model:
How our rubbish is sorted
In our building, rubbish is sorted into three groups. Plastic, glass and paper are put in the white bin, which is located next to the main door. Food waste is placed in the green bin. Everything else goes in the black bin. The bins are labelled clearly, so please check before you throw something away. The recyclable materials are collected every Tuesday by a group of local recyclers, who sell them to factories. Glass, which can be recycled many times, is taken to a plant in Soacha. Batteries and medicines must not be put in the bins; they are disposed of at the pharmacy on the corner. Thank you for helping!

14.title: A company I know
14.brief: Write a short profile of a company or business you know. Say what it does, how its products are made and who works there.
14.briefEs: Escribe el perfil de una empresa: qué hace, cómo se elaboran sus productos y quién trabaja allí.
criteria: Three passive verbs (are designed, is made, were founded).
Use who, which and whose in relative clauses.
One non-defining clause with commas.
14.model: Mochilas Wayuu Kanas is a small company that sells traditional bags online. It was founded in 2015 by Ana Epieyú, whose family has woven bags for generations. The bags are made by hand by a group of thirty women who live in La Guajira. Each bag, which can take up to three weeks to finish, is designed with traditional symbols. The cotton is bought from local farmers and the colours are chosen by the artisans. When the bags are ready, they are inspected, packed and sent to customers in more than ten countries. The company, which started with only two women, now supports many families in the community.

15.title: Recommendations for my school
15.brief: Write a short report for the director of your school or company with recommendations to improve something. Use passive modals.
15.briefEs: Escribe un informe breve con recomendaciones para mejorar tu colegio o empresa usando modales pasivos.
criteria: Five passive modals (should be improved, must be repaired, ought to be offered).
Clear structure with headings: Introduction, Problems, Recommendations.
Use “priority”, “to address” and “feasible”.
15.model:
Introduction
This report presents the results of a survey of 80 students about the school cafeteria.

Problems
Most students said the food is too expensive and there are not enough healthy options. The queues are very long at lunchtime, and the tables are often dirty.

Recommendations
Our first priority should be prices. Cheaper menus should be offered to students who have lunch every day. Healthy options like salads and fruit must be added. The problem of the queues could be addressed by opening a second counter, which seems feasible. The tables ought to be cleaned after every break. Finally, students' opinions should be collected every semester. If these changes are made, the cafeteria will be much more popular.

15.title: A tricky opinion
15.brief: Write a dialogue between two colleagues discussing a new rule at work. They use tag questions to check the other person agrees.
15.briefEs: Escribe un diálogo entre dos colegas que comentan una regla nueva usando tag questions.
criteria: Five tag questions with correct auxiliaries.
Two passive modals (should be changed, can't be ignored).
Use “surely”, “to bring up” or “to bear in mind”.
15.model:
Ana: The new rule about arriving at 7:30 is terrible, isn't it?
Luis: It's a bit early, isn't it? But we can leave at 4:30.
Ana: True, but they didn't ask us first, did they?
Luis: No, they didn't. Surely that should have been discussed with the team.
Ana: Exactly. And parents with small children will have problems, won't they?
Luis: That's a good point. It can't be ignored. We should bring it up at the meeting, shouldn't we?
Ana: Definitely. The schedule ought to be changed for people with kids.
Luis: Let's bear in mind that the boss is under pressure too.
Ana: You always see both sides, don't you?
Luis: I try!

15.title: Advice for new drivers
15.brief: Write a leaflet with recommendations for new drivers in your city. Use passive modals and impersonal recommendations.
15.briefEs: Escribe un folleto con recomendaciones para conductores nuevos en tu ciudad con modales pasivos.
criteria: Five passive modals (must be worn, should be checked).
Use “It is recommended / advisable that…” once.
Use “ought to”, “have got to” or “urgent”.
15.model:
Driving in Bogotá: tips for beginners
Driving in a big city can be stressful, but these tips will help.
• Seat belts must be worn by everyone in the car, including passengers in the back.
• Your tyres and brakes should be checked every month.
• The "pico y placa" rules have got to be respected, or you will be fined.
• Mobile phones must not be used while driving.
• Extra time ought to be allowed for traffic jams, especially when it rains.
• It is advisable that long trips are planned with an app like Waze.
• Motorbikes can appear from anywhere, so mirrors should be used constantly.
Remember: patience is the most important skill on the road!

16.title: My achievements this year
16.brief: Write a reflection about what you have achieved this year and what you achieved in specific moments.
16.briefEs: Escribe una reflexión sobre lo que has logrado este año y en momentos concretos.
criteria: Three present perfect sentences for achievements up to now.
Three simple past sentences with specific times.
Use “accomplishment”, “milestone” and “so far”.
16.model: This year has been one of the most productive of my life. So far, I have read twelve books in English and I have finished two online courses. I have also saved enough money for my first trip abroad. My biggest accomplishment happened in March, when I passed my driving test on the first try. In June, I ran my first 10K race, which was a real milestone for me because I used to hate running. In September, I got a promotion at work. Of course, not everything has been perfect. I haven't learned to cook yet, and I have spent too much time on my phone. But I'm proud of what I've achieved.

16.title: Goals for the next five years
16.brief: Write an email to a mentor or old teacher telling him or her what you have done since you last met and what you hope to have achieved in five years.
16.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un antiguo profesor contándole lo que has hecho y lo que esperas haber logrado en cinco años.
criteria: Use the present perfect and simple past for accomplishments.
Three future perfect verbs (will have finished).
Use “would like to have + past participle” once.
16.model:
Dear Professor Ríos,

I hope you remember me — I was in your economics class in 2021. I wanted to thank you, because your advice changed my life. Since then, I have finished my degree and I have started working at a bank. Last year, I also passed my first international finance exam.

I have big goals for the next five years. By 2030, I will have completed a master's degree, hopefully in Spain. I will have saved enough money to buy a small apartment, and I will have learned French as well. I would also like to have started my own financial advice business for small companies. I know it's ambitious, but you always told us to dream big.

Warm regards,
Juan Pablo Gil

16.title: Looking back, looking forward
16.brief: Write a blog post looking back on your English learning so far and setting realistic goals for the future.
16.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de blog sobre tu aprendizaje del inglés hasta ahora y metas realistas para el futuro.
criteria: Use “to look back on” and “in the long run”.
Two future perfect sentences with “by”.
One sentence with “would like to have + past participle”.
16.model: When I look back on my English journey, I'm surprised. Three years ago, I couldn't order a coffee in English. Since then, I have taken four courses, watched hundreds of series with subtitles and made friends from Canada and Australia. Last month, I had my first job interview in English, and I got the job! Of course, I've fallen short of some goals: I would like to have read more books, and my pronunciation still needs work. My new goals are realistic. By December, I will have finished the B2 course, and by next summer I will have taken the IELTS exam. In the long run, I want to use English every day without thinking about it.
